name: Ryokeijutsukanto (Japanese Kampo herbal formula)
short: Japanese adverse-event reports: one of 3 Kampo formulas most linked to pseudoaldosteronism (reporting odds ratio 5.5), which can cause low potassium. Case series of 4 women: no adverse effects.
text: Ryokeijutsukanto is a Japanese Kampo herbal formula used for dizziness from orthostatic dysregulation; the cited abstracts do not list its herbs. Its most serious reported harm is pseudoaldosteronism, which the cited database study calls a typical adverse effect of Kampo formulas and which a study of a different Kampo formula, yokukansan, describes, when caused by the licorice in yokukansan, as leading to high blood pressure, low potassium and muscle weakness, which may result in death; the database study links pseudoaldosteronism reports to the daily Glycyrrhiza (licorice) dose across formulas, but the cited abstracts do not say whether ryokeijutsukanto contains licorice. In the Japanese Adverse Drug Event Report database (April 2004 to November 2022; 210 pseudoaldosteronism reports among 2,471 Kampo reports with complete clinical data), ryokeijutsukanto was one of the three formulas most commonly associated with pseudoaldosteronism, with a reporting odds ratio of 5.5 (95% CI 1.4 to 21.9); these are spontaneous reports, which show a reporting association, not how often the problem occurs. Across Kampo formulas in that database, female sex, age 70 or over, body weight under 50 kg, diuretic use, high blood pressure, dementia, a higher daily Glycyrrhiza (licorice) dose and use for more than 14 days were associated with pseudoaldosteronism reports. In a case series of four women with dizziness from orthostatic dysregulation given ryokeijutsukanto, no adverse effects were observed. Apart from the diuretic finding, no interaction data were found in the cited sources.
